dossier.public_summary: The dip lands on the target star but its depth changes wildly between transits and between sectors, with some transits twice as deep as others. The 2.65-day period matches the star’s own spot rotation exactly and the star shows strong 300 ppm modulation at that period. Altogether the shape, unstable depth and rotation match are best explained by stellar spots and variability, not a planet.

reasons.why: difference imaging puts the dip on the target and rules out neighbours that could cause it (plausible_within_1px 0), so the signal is on-target, not a blend.
reasons.value: verdict on_target offset_arcsec 1.011 err_arcsec 1.218 offset_sigma 0.8296; suspects 32.7 sigma away

reasons.why: individual transit depths are highly inconsistent with a constant depth; multiple strong false-deep and false-shallow events drive the signal, not a stable planetary transit.
reasons.value: p_consistent 0.0 chi2 1913.0894616259006 dof 49 transit_depths outliers 1887 ppm 11.5 sigma (epoch 271), 1750 ppm 10.4 sigma (epoch 270) etc

reasons.why: depth changes dramatically even within the same pipeline product (TESS-SPOC), inconsistent with a planet; expected_share 0.1791 p_chance 0.9833 shows many spurious transits.
reasons.value: 1.271e-26 depth_change_pct 145.4; sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source TESS-SPOC p_constant 2.7047932547518096e-20 per sector 665, 410, 421, 376, 483 ppm

reasons.why: transit period is exactly the stellar rotation period (1.00x) with huge spot modulation; large phase-curve swing at same period is classic for spot/wave variability, not a planet.
reasons.value: rotation_d 2.634 signal_period_d 2.64507 signal_over_rotation 1.0042027334851937 signal_at_rotation_multiple 1; sector 43 amplitude_ppm 41504 sector 71 52010 phase_curve amplitude_ppm 306.3 ratio_to_depth 0.6212 chi2 765.2 dof 9

reasons.why: odd and even dips have significantly different depths, and the signal carries star-density mismatch (fit_log_density_ratio -2.524 star_density_penalty 1157 fit_b 0.8947 duration ratio 1.543 for rp 1.736 Rearth), favouring stellar variability/multiple spot states over a small planet.
independent classifier rates this planet-unlike (median planet 0.5, <0.1 only 10% planets), consistent with the positive variability/binary-like evidence.
